clue.text: By orchard, eat rotten type of food

indicators.note: rotten fruit has gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning not to eat the windfalls rotting under the orchard trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchard and the rotten fruit make you think of apples, but all three words before 'rotten' are raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbohydrate is a broad class of food, such as bread, pasta and potatoes.

clue.text: Dog left length of hair

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog has shed a clump of its fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a verb, the dog leaving hair behind, but it is only the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl is a single coiled lock, a length of hair.

clue.text: Annoyed in game, female ran off

explanation.surface: A player got annoyed during a match and a woman stormed away.
explanation.walkthrough: RU for rugby union is a stock crossword game; 'in' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled means put out or irritated, as in ruffled feathers.

clue.text: Appearing to knock when kept ready

blocks.note: an actor who is on is appearing on stage

explanation.surface: Someone shows up to knock at the door once everything is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: ON for 'appearing' comes from the theatre: the actor is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on tap is drawn straight from the barrel, so anything on tap is ready whenever wanted.

clue.text: Agreeable chaps are second in country

indicators.note: the S is put in the country's name

blocks.note: Yemen, in Arabia; it wraps round the S

explanation.surface: The friendliest men are found in second place in some nation's ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreeable' is doing double duty in spirit: yes-men are not pleasant, they simply agree with everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are people who always agree with their boss, so literally agreeable chaps.

clue.text: About a hundred dash for lounge

blocks.note: a dash is a short line

explanation.surface: Roughly a hundred people rush towards the lounge bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room to dash into, but it is the verb: to lie back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back at ease, which is to lounge.

clue.text: Little time to get skilled board

indicators.note: a little version of 'time' is its abbreviation, T

explanation.surface: With not much time, someone must become competent at a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a board game or a committee, but here it is the old sense of a table for meals, as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: A board is a flat surface for meals or work, which is a table.

clue.text: Road to a building hidden away

blocks.note: a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: A path leads to a building tucked out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a secluded building; in fact 'hidden away' is the definition, a past participle like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashed means put somewhere secret, that is hidden away.

clue.text: Starting to fall in line, backing overhaul

indicators.note: the start of 'fall' is its first letter
that letter goes in the line
the result runs backwards

blocks.note: a tier is a row or line; it wraps round the F

explanation.surface: Queue-jumpers start to fall into line, supporting a shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like support for the overhaul; it is an order to read the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a thorough overhaul, especially of a ship.

clue.text: Buck sat playing old instrument

indicators.note: the letters play about, rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A young man sat down to play an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' fits the musical surface perfectly, which hides its job as the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone.

clue.text: Evasive quality of a mule?

blocks.note: the plain reading: the trait of dodging capture or questions
the surface wants the stubborn animal; the setter means a mule as backless indoor footwear, and the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: A stubborn mule refusing to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is a red herring: a mule is also a backless slipper, so the quality of a mule is to be slipper-y.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipperiness is the quality of being evasive and hard to pin down.

clue.text: Designate river during a drink

indicators.note: the river flows during, that is inside, the drink

blocks.note: a pint; it wraps round the river

explanation.surface: Choosing someone while having a drink by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Po is the stock crossword river, as is the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: naming someone officially to a post is both.

clue.text: Salesperson - one in the saddle, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a pedaller sits in a bicycle saddle

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman on horseback, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The saddle suggests a horseman, but it belongs to a bicycle: the rider is a pedaller.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is an itinerant seller of small goods.

clue.text: Boy put hydrogen in cold liquor

indicators.note: hydrogen is put somewhere
namely inside the word for cold

blocks.note: cool = cold; it wraps round the H
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A lad in a lab adds hydrogen to chilled spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry fits a real fact: ethanol does contain hydrogen, which helps hide the symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, alcohol for short.

clue.text: Heavens! There's a weapon in the river

indicators.note: the weapon is placed in the river's name

blocks.note: the Dee, a British river; it wraps round the weapon
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm on spotting a gun in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' works as the exclamation of the surface and as the definition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me! and Heavens! are both mild exclamations of surprise or dismay.

clue.text: Ruled broadcast was wet

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so we get a sound

blocks.note: it rained = the weather was wet

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster announcing it had been a wet day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled' could be ruled lines or a verdict; the monarch's sense is the one needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a monarch holding the throne both governs and presides over the realm.

clue.text: In Lisbon, said to be little growth

indicators.note: the answer sits in the next words

explanation.surface: A report that something in Lisbon is supposedly small.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma between Lisbon and said does not stop the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a deliberately dwarfed tree, a little growth.

clue.text: Too chilled – so arranged for special neckwear?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Too cold outside, so someone sorts out a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: An old school tie is worn by former pupils of a British private school, and stands for the network of privilege they share.
explanation.definitionFit: An old school tie is a tie in a school's colours, special because only former pupils may wear it; the question mark admits the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Get rid of channel

blocks.note: first sense: a verb, to discard or abandon
second sense: a noun, a trench dug to carry water

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch off a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television, but it is the dug trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditch as a verb means discard, and as a noun a drainage channel.

clue.text: Notedly slow in regular government

indicators.note: the answer is in the following words

explanation.surface: A complaint that normal government moves remarkably slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' reads as 'notably', but means in musical notation: largo is a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Colourful worker coming from Ryde

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the letters of the town

blocks.note: anagram fodder; Ryde is a town on the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: A flamboyant labourer who hails from a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful' suggests a lively character, but a dyer literally works with colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer colours cloth for a living.

clue.text: Cuts on chest treated

indicators.note: the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: A nurse has dressed wounds on a patient's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes 'treated' look like first aid; it only reshuffles ON CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: small V-shaped nicks in an edge, like those on a tally stick.

clue.text: Gangling youth leader telephoned before

indicators.note: the leader of 'youth' is its first letter
the phone call comes before that letter

explanation.surface: A lanky youth club leader had phoned earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth leader' looks like a job title; it just means the first letter of 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes someone tall and long-limbed, which is gangling.

clue.text: Tablet, one back in soup, is hot stuff

indicators.note: the tablet and one are turned back to front
that result goes inside the soup

blocks.note: chowder is a thick soup; it wraps round the reversed piece

explanation.surface: A medicine dropped into soup turns out to be fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Tablet' tempts you to read it as the definition; 'hot stuff' at the end is the real one, with 'is' as the link. Chowder is a thick, creamy soup, often of clams.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the ground dried peppers are spicy-hot, taken literally rather than as slang for something desirable.
